facts.F1: Bug 6654: Restore and Clear Database fail on Windows with SQLite ("file is being used by another process"). On Windows (and macOS) with the SQLite provider, Database Management -> Restore Backup always fails with System.IO.IOException: The process cannot access the file LighthouseAppContext.db because it is being used by another process. Clear Database fails the same way. Additional request: warn that backups do not include the encryption key, check before restoring, and allow starting anyway; maintainer decision: allow restoring without the unreadable credentials so the app starts and the user re-enters them.

facts.F16: SQLite restore and clear write through the SQLite online backup API (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite SqliteConnection.BackupDatabase) instead of replacing or deleting files. Restore: source is a Pooling=False connection on the staged backup .db in the extract directory (SQLite applies a legacy backup's -wal when it opens it); destination is a new Pooling=False connection on the live connection string with PRAGMA busy_timeout=10000. Clear: source is an empty Data Source=:memory: connection. The live .db, -wal and -shm files are never replaced or deleted, so every open connection, pooled or leaked, reads the new pages, and journal_mode stays WAL. RecycleConnection, migrations and seeding still follow in DatabaseManagementService. Owner: SqliteDatabaseManagementProvider.

facts.F18: Postgres staging: PostgresDatabaseManagementProvider.StageBackup creates a scratch database named after the live one with the suffix _restore_check (psql CREATE DATABASE, after DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS WITH (FORCE)), runs pg_restore --table=WorkTrackingSystemConnectionOption --table=OAuthCredentials into it, and its IStagedBackup opens an NpgsqlConnection to it and drops it WITH (FORCE) on DisposeAsync. Rejected: checking after the restore (breaks nothing-is-changed), parsing pg_restore SQL output (COPY escaping is brittle), skipping the check on Postgres (breaks P2).

facts.F26: Checker mapping: the restore, check, copy and removal state machine (P2, P3 safety) is a finite state model checked with Quint (quint verify on the Apalache backend, exhaustive at the reachable depth of 5 steps because every run settles within 3 transitions). TLA+/TLC is not needed: there is no temporal or fairness claim. Agda is not selected: no claim needs a proof beyond the finite model. The SQLite page-level behaviour behind P1 (an open connection reads the pages the backup API wrote) is a property of SQLite, not of this design, so it is not modelled; the S3 oracle observes it at runtime. Liveness is not applicable: each operation is one synchronous, bounded request that never waits on another party (gate acquisition returns at once), so no progress claim depends on fairness.
